Its small cell footprint (dominant_pixel_fraction=0.0206) is well-suited for close-range residential capacity absorption but may not fully compensate for USID_00's broader macro reach in the coverage hole fringe.
load_geographic_context.notes: No hospitals, emergency services, or major transit hubs are visibly identifiable within the specific USID_00 dominant footprint in the real map. The area is predominantly suburban residential with road corridors. The coverage gap in the NW fringe falls along a road corridor which may affect vehicular users but is not classified as critical infrastructure.

key_findings_for_stage4: Coverage holes (11.54%, 3 pixels) are geographically localized to the NW fringe of USID_00's dominant area along a diagonal arterial road corridor — users on this road segment will face a true signal gap; however, this is a road corridor rather than critical infrastructure (no hospital or emergency services identified).

The central residential core (majority of USID_00's 26 dominant pixels) lies in an interference-limited SINR regime (dominant_area_impact_regime='mostly_mild'), meaning USID_27 and USID_29 are already competing strongly and handover quality degradation will be limited for the bulk of users.

USID_27 micro tower (20m, NW position) is well-placed geographically to serve the dense residential immediately adjacent to USID_00, but its limited height and 2-band profile (no Band_700) may reduce building penetration for users in the NW residential blocks.

No critical infrastructure (hospital, emergency, transit hub) identified within USID_00's compact dominant footprint — this absence prevents constraint C2 from triggering and keeps overall severity at a lower level.

All backup towers are well-distributed around the USID_00 footprint (NW: USID_27, E: USID_29, SW: USID_41, S: USID_37, SE: USID_31), providing multi-directional geographic coverage with no single backup failure point; load distribution risk is low across all sectors.

The exact 3-pixel location of coverage holes within the NW fringe is inferred from the dominance map boundary and neighbor signal patterns — precise street-level positioning requires drive-test validation.
